paragraphs: If you are willing to confirm the set values and ranges before calibration, to isolate energy and apply lockout and tagout before repair, and to write every test and replacement into the records, this occupation is worth learning more about; people who adjust by feel and hand the work over rarely last.

If you can accept 74% of working days spent outdoors in all kinds of weather, 36% every day in extremely hot or cold temperatures and 53% every day in a non-climate-controlled indoor or site environment, and can accept 39% of weeks over 40 hours (with emergency repairs and standby on top), this job will use that tolerance every day; people who only want to work in a climate-controlled office will not adapt.

If you are willing to keep disassembling, assembling and adjusting with your hands (59% almost continuously handling tools and parts) and accept entering confined spaces 29% every day and working in awkward postures 35% at least once a week, this job suits you; people who dislike hands-on work and only want to read data will struggle.

If you are willing to deal frequently with users, dispatchers and crews (95% have face-to-face discussions every day, 74% make phone calls every day and 74% are in continuous contact with others) and can calmly handle repair pressure and dissatisfaction (27% meet unpleasant or impatient people every day), this job can be done long term; people who dislike external communication will not adapt.

If you are willing to isolate and report first when you find a leak, an illegal connection, a failed meter or a site hazard, and then repair and re-test to procedure, this occupation is worth learning more about; papering over a hazard as a small problem can end in loss of gas or power supply, inaccurate metering or personal injury.

Situations where this is not a good choice: being unwilling to confirm set values and ranges before calibration, being unwilling to isolate energy and apply lockout and tagout before repair, being unwilling to fill in test and maintenance records, being unable to accept outdoor and confined space work, tending to skip re-testing under pressure, or tending to keep using something after finding a hazard. Boundary: the exercises and judgments on this page are only for self-checking and do not constitute hiring standards, qualification determinations or work authorization; for gas, electricity, pressure vessels and special equipment work, follow the rules of your organization and the competent authorities.

How to try it: for a fictional scenario (during an inspection at a residential gas pressure regulating station the outlet pressure fluctuates and there is a slight smell, downstream users complain about unstable supply, and there is a maintenance window the next day) write a one-page handling plan, including the isolation and guarding sequence, the basis for testing and judgment, whether supply must be shut off and who must be notified, the repair and re-test steps, and who needs to confirm and how it will be documented.

Before starting, confirm: you can break a work cycle into three categories, installation and testing, calibration and leak testing, and fault handling and records, and explain whether each item is based on technical specifications, calibration procedures or a site instruction; and you can state before deciding which parameters you have measured and which still need verification or confirmation from a supervisor.

Note: this page does not cover mechanical engineer or calibration technician content. Mechanical engineers are responsible for design and technical solutions, and calibration technicians focus on calibrating measuring equipment against standards and evaluating uncertainty; this occupation focuses on on-site installation, repair and maintenance of mechanical regulating and control devices and on testing and recording to specification, and the three have different authorization and outputs.

In one sentence: this is a job whose core is confirming specifications and safety conditions first, then disassembling, assembling, calibrating and leak testing, delivering on measured data and documenting every test and replacement; it suits people with steady hands, who are willing to work outdoors and in confined spaces, can communicate clearly with users and dispatchers and take on metering and safety responsibility.

Installation and testing, calibration and leak testing, and repair and records are overlapping editorial work surfaces, not a fixed full process for every position; work is divided by actual equipment task qualification.
Installation and testing records, and fault and metering deviation judgment

Editorial installation and testing chain: check the specification and work order, install or test under the actual authorization, check readings and pressure, and record problems and results; this is a supplemental task and does not guarantee that every position handles all meters, gas and valve objects.
Calibration and test records, and leak and set value conclusions

Editorial calibration and leak testing chain: check the range, settings and permitted deviation for the specific device and method, record the test and submit it to the position that actually holds the authority; this is not simultaneous calibration of four parameters on every device or statutory verification authority.

Editorial repair chain: check the applicable energy procedure and authorization, disassemble, repair, lubricate or replace parts, test and record to the specific procedure, and hand over. U.S. 1910.147 is limited to the hazardous energy of equipment maintenance within its coverage; it excludes generation, transmission and distribution under the exclusive control of electric utilities and related metering facilities, construction and so on, and electrical hazards are covered separately by subpart S. Applicable repairs are controlled and verified by an authorized employee under the energy procedure; lockout and tagout is not uniform for all tasks in all jurisdictions.

This page compares this occupation with adjacent occupations item by item across seven dimensions: core purpose, main objects and basis, core process, main outputs, responsible party, admission and permits, and conclusion boundary. Adjacent positions are all in equipment or engineering roles, but engineering responsibility for design solutions, calibration of measuring equipment against standards, manufacture and installation of boilers and pressure vessels, installation of piping systems and steam systems, and repair of motors and power tools do not transfer just because the positions are adjacent; when comparing, check the position's actual duties item by item against the seven dimensions in the comparison table on this page.

Core purposes of adjacent occupations: mechanical engineers are responsible for the design, analysis and technical solutions of mechanical equipment and systems; calibration technicians calibrate measuring equipment against standards and evaluate uncertainty; boilermakers make and install boilers, pressure vessels and tanks; plumbers, pipefitters and steamfitters install and repair piping and steam systems; and motor and power tool repairers repair motors, power tools and related electrical components.

Installing, repairing and maintaining mechanical regulating and control devices is the occupational definition; specific metering, electrical and gas supply tasks are divided by qualification and authorization, and the job title does not guarantee that all systems are reliable.

Objects and basis of adjacent occupations: design codes and engineering calculations (mechanical engineers), measurement standards and calibration procedures (calibration technicians), boiler and pressure vessel manufacturing codes (boilermakers), piping and steam system drawings and codes (plumbers and so on), and motor and power tool schematics and repair manuals (motor repairers).

Electricity meters, pressure regulators, thermostats, safety valves and flow valves and so on; the basis is the actual technical specifications, drawings and testing data, with statutory verification and special equipment rules checked separately where applicable.

Processes of adjacent occupations: design calculation and drawing production (mechanical engineers), comparison against standards and issuing calibration results (calibration technicians), manufacture and installation to code with pressure testing (boilermakers), pipe layout and connection to drawings with pressure testing (plumbers and so on), and disassembly of windings and components with repair and testing (motor repairers).
The three editorial work surfaces can overlap, and installation, calibration, repair and stopping or restoring supply are not treated as a mandatory sequence for every position.

Outputs of adjacent occupations: design documents and technical solutions (mechanical engineers), calibration certificates and uncertainty statements (calibration technicians), boiler and pressure vessel installation and pressure test records (boilermakers), piping installation and pressure test records (plumbers and so on), and motor and tool repair and test records (motor repairers).
Installation and testing records, calibration and test records, repair and replacement records, meter reading and work order data, and hazard and illegal connection reports.

Responsible parties of adjacent occupations: mechanical engineers are responsible for the engineering correctness of design solutions, calibration technicians for calibration results and traceability, boilermakers for the manufacturing and installation quality of pressure parts, plumbers and so on for piping system installation quality and pressure testing, and motor repairers for the quality of motor and tool repair.

China's urban gas regulations are limited to the scope of Article 2, and Article 15 requires the operation, maintenance and emergency repair personnel of operating enterprises to pass professional training and assessment; Article 20 requires planned maintenance shutdowns to be notified 48 hours in advance and emergency measures to be taken and notified promptly when supply is affected suddenly, which are two different cases. Equipment repair experience does not substitute for the operator's responsibility or the authority to stop and restore supply. China's Special Equipment Safety Law is limited to equipment in the catalogue, with Articles 13 and 14 on education and related qualifications and Article 39 on periodic verification, inspection and records for accessories; Annex 2 of No. 41 of 2021 specifies safety valve verification F, so not all valves can be called pressure equipment certificates. Unit licensing, work qualification and inspection and testing qualification are checked separately.

Specification, connection, testing, energy control and hazard records are editorial observation points; statutory verification, permits and stopping and restoring supply must each be checked separately, and they are not a uniform six-item procedure.
Judgment one: are the specification and range confirmed?

Check the size, range and test criteria against the actual technical specifications; statutory verification applicability is checked separately, and this round did not obtain evidence that relying on experience necessarily causes re-testing problems.
Judgment two: are the installation and connections in place?
Installation and connections are checked against the actual drawings, specifications and permits; defects may affect commissioning, but it is not said that rework necessarily happens every time.
Judgment three: are the calibration and set values acceptable?

Check against the parameters and methods that actually need calibration for the device, and do not uniformly calibrate four parameters item by item or use a uniform number of points. Articles 9, 10 and 20 of China's Metrology Law: compulsory verification follows the applicable use and catalogue and is carried out by statutory or authorized bodies and assessed personnel according to the verification system and procedures; general function adjustment, calibration or repair records do not automatically replace compulsory verification or the statutory data used in disputes. The specific instrument catalogue, procedures and body scope are checked separately.
Judgment four: have the leak and function re-tests been done?
Leak and set value testing are checked against the specific specifications and applicable procedures, and general re-testing does not replace statutory inspection or permission to restore.
Judgment five: have the applicable energy control and verification been checked?

paragraphs: The six adjacent directions differ in object and authorization: adjacent positions are all in equipment, engineering or metering roles, but engineering responsibility for design solutions, calibration of and traceability to standards for measuring equipment, manufacture and installation of pressure parts, installation of piping and steam systems, and repair of motors and industrial machinery do not transfer just because the positions are adjacent; when comparing, check the position's actual duties item by item against the seven dimensions in the comparison table on this page.

Evidence note: the occupational scope and adjacent relationships in this table are based on O*NET related occupations and the 2018 SOC classification; tasks and work context are based on the O*NET 49-9012.00 occupation details; U.S. wages and employment are based on the exact occupation scope of the O*NET national wages page and summary page (2025 wage data, 2024 employment and 2024—2034 projections), together with the 2025—2035 scope of the BLS Occupational Outlook Handbook installation, maintenance and repair occupations group and its May 2025 median wage (a broader scope). Adjacent relationships do not mean qualifications transfer, that positions are interchangeable, or that gas, electrical or special equipment work authorization can be transferred.

The table below places this occupation and five adjacent occupations on the same set of dimensions: for each direction it first states the core work and outputs, then the key differences from this occupation, and finally when that direction is a better choice.

Mechanical engineers are responsible for the engineering correctness and technical indicators of design solutions and usually do not carry out on-site disassembly, assembly and calibration; this occupation installs, calibrates and repairs to technical specifications and drawings and delivers on measured results.

If you would rather do design calculations and technical solutions, look at the mechanical engineers direction; if you would rather work on site installing, calibrating and leak testing and deliver measured data, look at this occupation.
Be responsible for the design, analysis and technical solutions of mechanical equipment and systems, producing design documents and technical solutions.
Mechanical Engineers

Calibration technicians calibrate measuring equipment against standards and determine traceability in a controlled environment, producing calibration certificates; this occupation installs, adjusts and tests regulating and control devices on site, and its test conclusions serve equipment function and metering accuracy rather than issuing a metrological standard traceability conclusion.

If you would rather focus on measurement standards, uncertainty and calibration certificates, look at the calibration technicians direction; if you would rather handle device faults and set values at the user's site, look at this occupation.
Calibrate measuring equipment against measurement standards, evaluate uncertainty and issue calibration results.
Calibration Technologists and Technicians

Boilermakers deal with the manufacture and installation of pressure parts, working mainly by welding, fitting up and pressure testing; this occupation deals with metering and regulating control devices and works mainly by disassembly, assembly, calibration and leak testing, and does not include the manufacture of pressure parts.
If you would rather manufacture and install pressure parts, look at the boilermakers direction; if you would rather install and repair metering and regulating devices, look at this occupation.
Manufacture and install boilers, pressure vessels and tanks to code and complete pressure testing and delivery.
Boilermakers

Plumbers and similar trades deal with the pipe network itself and deliver mainly system installation and pressure testing; this occupation installs metering and regulating devices on the network, focusing on set values and metering accuracy, and does not carry responsibility for pipe network layout or system pressure testing.

If you would rather lay pipes, make connections and pressure test systems, look at the plumbers and similar direction; if you would rather commission devices and metering accuracy, look at this occupation.
Install and repair water supply, drainage, gas and steam piping systems to drawings and complete pressure testing and flushing.
Plumbers, Pipefitters, and Steamfitters

Motor and power tool repairers work mainly with motor windings, power tools and electrical components, with work concentrated in a repair workshop; this occupation deals with on-site metering and regulating control devices and requires visiting user sites and handling supply shutdown and restoration and hazard reporting.
If you would rather repair motors and power tools in a workshop, look at that direction; if you would rather go to sites to handle devices and user problems, look at this occupation.
Repair motors, power tools and related electrical components, producing repair and test records.
Electric Motor, Power Tool, and Related Repairers

Industrial machinery mechanics serve the production equipment itself and line availability, and their work is constrained by the production plan and shutdown windows; this occupation serves utility metering and pressure regulating devices, and its work is constrained by user energy use and maintenance windows and involves metering accuracy and supply stop and restore procedures.

If you would rather be responsible for line equipment and shutdown repair organisation, look at the industrial machinery mechanics direction; if you would rather be responsible for on-site work on metering and regulating devices, look at this occupation.
Repair and maintain factory production equipment and industrial machinery, producing repair and condition records.
Industrial Machinery Mechanics

If you are torn between two directions, first run a small experiment with a fictional work order: write a one-page status statement (equipment model and specification, the testing or calibration items to be completed, on-site safety conditions and who needs to confirm), then see whether you would rather be responsible for on-site installation and calibration conclusions, for design solutions, for calibration traceability, for pressure parts or piping systems, or for motor and industrial machinery repair.

values: Fictional work order materials (exercise input)

Fictional scenario: during a patrol at a residential gas pressure regulating station the outlet pressure fluctuates and there is a slight smell, downstream users complain about unstable supply, and there is a maintenance window the next morning but a gas use peak in the afternoon.

Materials provided: excerpts of the regulating station's technical specifications and set value requirements; outlet pressure and flow records for the last three days; the site patrol record and a description of where the smell is; the verification cycle list for the meters; a diagram of the upstream and downstream isolation valve positions.

Materials not provided: the exact location of the smell source and concentration test results, the extent of the impact on downstream users' gas use, the list of available spare parts, and whether supply must be shut off and the approval process for that. If these conditions are needed in the exercise, state your assumptions and who you need to confirm them with.
Task requirements

Write a one-page handling plan: including the on-site safety judgment and guarding sequence, the testing and isolation steps, whether supply must be shut off and who to notify, the repair and replacement plan, the conditions for re-testing and restoring supply, and who needs to confirm and how it will be documented.
The plan must state which parameters you have measured and which are still assumptions, and explain whether it relies on technical specifications, verification procedures or on-site observation.
Reference deliverable (derivable from the prompt)

The plan should include: current status judgment (the relationship between the outlet pressure fluctuation and the smell, and possible regulator or valve problems), safety handling (evacuation and guarding, ventilation and testing, isolation and depressurisation), option comparison (the risk and time of on-site setting adjustment versus disassembly and replacement), re-testing and restoration (re-test set values and leakage to specification and record them), communication and documentation (notifying dispatch and users, seeking approval for the supply shutdown, recording the handling process) and risk notes (the smell source and concentration are unconfirmed).
The reference deliverable lists only the elements that should be included and does not require the same wording as the example; being able to explain the basis for your judgment is enough.
Boundaries and conclusions that cannot be inferred

This exercise only tests safety procedure awareness, the calibration and leak testing approach and document organisation ability; it does not assess the safety or compliance of real equipment, and does not constitute hiring, a qualification judgment or handling advice for real work.
Do not use operating data, repair or incident material from real enterprises; for real work, follow the rules of your organization and the competent authorities.

Next step: if you are willing to continue with the first six steps, the next step is to complete a loop from testing to re-testing under compliant conditions (such as a training course, a training rig or de-identified materials) and have an experienced repair worker review it; if a step clearly drains you, narrow the direction first and verify again.

entries.answer: After being dispatched to site they first check the work order and equipment specifications and confirm safety conditions, then install or test metering and regulating devices, calibrate for pressure, temperature, flow and level and adjust set values into the specified range, and test valves and regulators for leaks and setting accuracy; if a fault is found they isolate energy, disassemble and repair and replace failed parts, and after a successful re-test restore operation and gas or power supply, and finally fill in test results, materials used and repair records and complete handover.
entries.question: What do control and valve installers and repairers do every day?

entries.answer: Calibration technicians calibrate measuring equipment against measurement standards in a controlled environment, evaluate uncertainty and issue calibration conclusions; this occupation installs, adjusts and tests regulating and control devices on site, handles leaks, set values and functional faults, and its test conclusions serve equipment function and metering accuracy without replacing a metrological standard traceability conclusion.
entries.question: What is the difference between control and valve installers and repairers and calibration technicians?

entries.answer: Some collection and recording tasks will be taken over by tools (remote metering and pressure regulating data collection, anomaly and leak warnings, work order dispatch, spare part and verification cycle reminders, record archiving), but judging whether a device needs disassembly, how to isolate and stop or restore supply when there is a leak or metering anomaly, how to ensure safety in confined spaces and when energy is not fully isolated, and deciding at the user's site whether to continue working still rest with positions that hold the authority; the employment scope on this page cannot be used to infer the degree of replacement.
entries.question: Will AI replace control and valve installers and repairers?

entries.answer: Remote metering data collection and anomaly warning, work order dispatch and route optimisation, spare part and verification cycle reminders, digital archiving of calibration readings and maintenance records, and model-specific testing item lists; tasks that require on-site judgment of device condition, deciding supply stop and restore when there is a leak or metering anomaly, and working in confined spaces and under energy isolation are not easily fully automated.
entries.question: Which tasks are most easily assisted?

entries.answer: Making isolation and handling decisions at the scene of a leak, overpressure or metering anomaly, ensuring work safety where energy is not fully isolated, judging whether a device can continue in use, completing calibration and re-testing to specification and being responsible for the conclusions, and turning test and replacement records into traceable evidence.
